payload.label: Compare movement
payload.description: Derives keypoint tracks, phase ranges, source-to-source alignments, and movement comparisons from source artifacts through open motion process profiles.

payload.domain_contract: Tennis stroke names, basketball shot names, dance phases, walking gait phases, and future movement vocabularies are phase labels/taxonomy refs in records or process profiles, not package code.

sources_contract.shape: array of source refs with artifact_ref

options_contract.motion_command: optional object with process_descriptor and process_profile for the motion command to run through compute.process
options_contract.process_profile: open data for provider, model, keypoint schema, phase taxonomy refs, comparison metrics, credential handle refs, runtime, lanes, and output policy; sport/domain/model choices are not code branches

payload.runner_contract: compute.process or compute.process_session as configured by workflow data
payload.process_profile_contract: profile data carries model, keypoint schema, phase taxonomy, runtime, and opaque credential handle choices

payload.track_contract: Keypoint/pose payloads live in track_artifact_ref, not inline UI records.

payload.phase_contract: Phase labels such as tennis stroke, basketball shot, dance, walking, or any future movement domain labels are data.

payload.alignment_contract: Alignments link two or more source spans through refs and transform artifacts; renderers consume this record but do not own truth.

payload.comparison_contract: Movement comparison summaries cite tracks, phases, and alignments; no renderer-local JSON is the comparison authority.

payload.details_contract: optional machine-readable command/process details; never stores fabricated motion comparisons

payload.name: motion-analysis-ingest-reference
payload.description: Run a caller-supplied reference media ref through the motion perception process, translate its self-describing descriptor into reference records, and write each produced record.

input_contract.notes: The caller supplies the reference media ref. This action stages request.json, runs perception/orchestrate.sh, runs ingest/make-reference-records-from-descriptor.py, and writes each produced record.

argv: set -e; tar -xf perception.tar; : "${MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT:?MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT must be set on the host to the provisioned perception vendor root (onnx models + static ffmpeg + sp/ wheels)}"; export MATCH_FFMPEG="$MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT/ffmpeg"; export PYTHONPATH="$MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT/sp:perception"; for m in yolo11n-pose.onnx jointbdoe_coco_l.onnx clip_vitb32_visual.onnx; do ln -sf "$MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT/$m" "perception/$m"; done; exec bash perception/orchestrate.sh clip.mp4 . "$1" "$2" perception/yolo11n-pose.onnx

payload.description: Run a caller-supplied SUBJECT clip ref through the SAME motion perception process as ingest-reference, TORCH-FREE on the bare host (backend=onnx). The perception SCRIPTS arrive as a small mounted stored_bytes tar (perception.tar); the MODELS (3 onnx checkpoints + static ffmpeg + the numpy/onnxruntime/Pillow wheels under sp/) are NOT package bytes — they live in a host-provisioned filesystem vendor root selected by env DATA ($MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT, L089/L123: model weights are an immutable shared substrate, never per-app log/CAS bytes), mirroring ingest-reference's JOINTBDOE_VENDOR pattern. The only per-request blob is the clip. Emits the motion-clip-descriptor.v1 (command-output.json) and the keypoints (command-output.kp.json) BOTH as addressed_chunks; their integrity_hashes are the subject_descriptor_ref / subject_pose_ref that motion-comparison.run-comparison consumes. Subject leg of the live pipeline (upload->pose->describe->match->render): RETURNS the two CAS refs in its step output, writes no reference records. Fail-closed: run_perception REQUIRES rc==0 + the declared output, and MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT must be set (:? guard) — a missing vendor root / person / model / heading surfaces a hard error, never a partial descriptor. | Emits a comparison-ready record (subject refs + pass-through reference context) so a describe->match trigger can dispatch run-comparison with zero human input.

input_contract.notes: clip_ref = an engine-minted CAS blob_ref to the uploaded subject video ({hash:...}). request_id = the job/correlation id (label only). The onnx pose checkpoint is the mounted perception/yolo11n-pose.onnx (not user data). Result: step output.outputs.0.integrity_hash = subject_descriptor_ref, output.outputs.1.integrity_hash = subject_pose_ref.

payload.name: motion-analysis-materialize-index
payload.description: Build a matcher-readable reference index (index.tar in engine CAS) from a motion-reference-clip record set, for ANY number of references. Mount records.json + the N records' keypoint blobs DIRECTLY (each kp_cas is a record-pinned, cross-workflow-readable CAS blob), copy them into staged/0.kp.json..(N-1).kp.json in records order, place each record's kp at the materializer's key path, materialize the index dir (fail-closed kp verify), and tar it. The output index.tar integrity_hash is the reference_index_ref motion-comparison.run-comparison mounts. PER-RECORD DIRECT MOUNT (not a pre-built kp_bundle tar): a workflow's addressed_chunks OUTPUT only becomes cross-workflow-readable after a CAS snapshot, so a transient intermediate kp_bundle blob is NOT reliably readable by the next dispatch; but each kp_cas blob is referenced by a committed reference-clip record and is therefore immediately readable. N = the count of static kp mounts below = reference-set DATA (re-author the mounts list to change the default reference set; the engine has no dynamic-N-mount primitive). A single reference is just a 1-mount case (extra kp_refs absent → fail-closed).

input_contract.notes: records_ref = a CAS blob_ref to the motion-reference-clip records ({records:[...]} or a records array). kp_refs = an ORDERED array of CAS blob_refs ([{hash},...]) to the N records' keypoint blobs (each = a reference-clip record's kp_cas = the addressed_chunks integrity_hash from ingest-reference perception), in the SAME order as the records array. Mounted directly at <i>.kp.json. All are engine-minted, record-pinned CAS addresses.

argv: set -e; tar -xf scripts.tar; : "${MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT:?MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT must be set on the host to the provisioned vendor root (sp/ wheels: numpy/scipy/scikit-learn)}"; export PYTHONPATH="$MATCH_VENDOR_ROOT/sp"; mkdir -p staged index; cp [0-9]*.kp.json staged/; python3 ingest/place-engine-staged-kp.py --records-json records.json --staged-dir staged --out-dir index; python3 ingest/build-index-artifact.py --records-json records.json --engine-staged --index-dir index --out-tar index.tar

payload.name: motion-analysis-publish-reference-index
payload.description: Publish a DISCOVERABLE motion-reference-index record for an already-built index.tar so a live consumer can FIND the index's CAS hash instead of being handed it. Runs ingest/make-reference-index-record.py over the mounted reference-clip records + the dispatch input and writes the produced motion-reference-index record by its own address. A consumer reads that record, takes index_ref_hash, and dispatches motion-comparison.run-comparison. The whole dispatch input is mounted as request.json and read via --input-json, so an ABSENT optional (index_id/comparison_spec_ref/index_byte_len) never becomes a null-bound argv slot (FE_CODEC_ERROR).

input_contract.notes: index_ref_hash = the index.tar CAS multihash (run-comparison's reference_index_ref.hash). records_ref = a CAS blob_ref ({hash}) to the motion-reference-clip records ({records:[...]} or [...]) the index was built from. The whole dispatch input is mounted as request.json and read via --input-json; the scalar fields are NOT bound into separate argv slots.

argv: set -e; tar -xf scripts.tar; python3 ingest/make-reference-index-record.py --input-json request.json --reference-records-json records.json --output-json out.json

payload._activation: is_active IS the front-door switch — a comparison-request write auto-starts the whole pipeline (describe-subject -> comparison-ready -> [match] -> result -> [render] -> render), zero code. Fail-closed: fires only when the subject clipRef is a real CAS hash.
